newsitem.title: CHINA: HK blue chips surge to record in morning, then fall.
newsitem.headline: HK blue chips surge to record in morning, then fall.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index jumped to a record high in early trade on Thursday, the first trading day under Chinese rule, before falling later as handover enthusiasm was brushed aside and investors focused on property.
The blue chip index soared 166.82 points, or 1.10 percent, to an all-time high of 15,363.61 points minutes after the opening bell rang.
It later succumbed to profit-taking to trade down 123.78 points, or 0.81 percent, at 15,073.01 points at late morning.
"The market was artificially pumped up," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at Nava SC Securities.
"But here comes the realisation that we still have this overhang about what is going to happen to the property market."
Property stocks led the market down after Hong Kong's new government said on Tuesday it would increase housing supply to deal with escalating real estate prices.
Shares in Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd tumbled HK$2.00 to HK$74.50 while Henderson Land Development Co Ltd was off HK$1.75 at HK$67.00 and Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd was down HK$2.75 at HK$90.50.
"Handover fever is coming to an end and investors are taking a break in the short run before taking new positions," said Edwin Cheung, a senior sales manager at Taiwan Securities.
"Profit-taking is a bit hectic but we expect support at the 15,000 level," he added.

Meanwhile, red chip stocks welcomed a new era under China with firm gains. The Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporations Index was up 39.08 points, or 1.13 percent, at 3,508.40 after surging to an early high of 3,561.23.
Turnover was a hefty HK$7.27 billion after the first hour of trade.
Banking stocks made hefty gains in morning trade on Thursday with HSBC Holdings Plc jumping to a record high of HK$239.00 before paring its gains to trade up HK$2.00 at HK$235.00.
Hang Seng Bank Ltd also hit an all-time high at HK$116.00 before trading up HK$2.50 at HK$113.00.
